content: Hey everyone! Good morning.
Morning! Anyone up for a standup?
I'm in. Just finished deploying the latest build.
Morning all. I pushed some new mockups to the shared folder.
Nice! I'll take a look after lunch.
The test suite is green on main btw
Great, I'll promote to staging then
Quick question — should we use the new design system tokens for the dashboard?
Yes absolutely. I already started migrating the sidebar.
Make sure to update the snapshot tests if you change the sidebar
Heads up: I'm rotating the API keys at 2pm. There might be a brief blip.
Noted. I'll pause my E2E tests around then.
Should we document the key rotation process somewhere?
Good call. I'll add it to the runbook after lunch.
Anyone else having trouble with the staging DB? Queries are super slow.
Yeah I noticed that too. Looks like the vacuum job didn't run last night.
I can take a look at the cron config if you want
That would be great, thanks Alice
New color palette proposal in the design channel btw. Would love feedback.
Oh nice, I like the darker accents
Same. The contrast ratios look much better.
Thanks! I ran them all through the WCAG checker this time
Deploy to staging is done. v2.4.1 is live there now.
Running smoke tests... one sec
All green! Ship it.
Awesome. Great work everyone.
Pushing to prod in 10 minutes. Last chance to object.
No objections from me
Go for it
Full send
Prod deploy complete. Monitoring dashboards look clean.
Perfect. I'm heading out for the day. See you all tomorrow!
Later Alice!
Bye! Great day everyone.
See ya. I'll keep an eye on the metrics overnight.
Oh wait, one more thing — the weekly report is due Friday. Who's writing it this week?
I think it's Dana's turn
Yep, I've got it. Will send a draft Thursday afternoon.
Cool, thanks Dana
Actually still here — just wanted to say the new onboarding flow metrics look great. 40% improvement in completion rate.
That's amazing! The simplified form really made a difference.
We should write a blog post about that
Agreed. Good data to share externally.
Ok NOW I'm actually leaving. Night everyone!
Night!
Night!
Goodnight!
Alright I'm out too. Catch everyone tomorrow.
Same. Signing off.
One last thing — I updated the Figma with the final icon set. Link in the design channel.
Thanks Dana, bookmarked it.
Ok goodnight for real this time
Morning team. Prod metrics from overnight look solid. Zero errors.
Morning! That's what I like to hear.
Hey all. Coffee acquired, ready to go.
Good morning! I have the weekly report draft if anyone wants to review before I send it.
Sure, drop the link
It's in the shared drive under Reports/Week-12.md
Reading it now... looks good. Maybe add a line about the onboarding metrics?
Oh good call, I forgot to include that. Adding now.
Also mention the staging DB fix from yesterday. That was a real save.
Agreed. Alice's cron fix prevented a lot of headaches.
Aw thanks. It was a one-liner honestly.
The best fixes usually are
So what's the plan for today? Sprint planning?
Yeah, we have the planning meeting at 10. Did everyone groom the backlog?
I added estimates to the infra tickets last night
Design tickets are all sized and have mockups attached
I've got the test tickets ready too. A few need acceptance criteria though.
Let's finalize those in the meeting. I'll pull up the board.
Quick thing before that — the SSL cert for api.staging expires next week. I'll renew it today.
Good catch. Those expiry emails always end up in spam somehow.
We should automate cert renewal with Let's Encrypt
It's on my list. Just haven't had time to set up certbot.
Can we also talk about the mobile responsive issues in planning? I filed three bugs yesterday.
Yeah I saw those. The sidebar collapse is definitely broken on tablets.
I'll pick those up. Should be quick CSS fixes.
Thanks Alice. I included screenshots in each ticket.
Meeting in 5. Everyone ready?
Ready
Yep
Let's do it
Good meeting. I think we have a solid sprint ahead.
Agreed. I like that we kept scope manageable this time.
Famous last words
lol Charlie always the optimist
He's not wrong though. Remember sprint 14?
We don't talk about sprint 14.
Anyway, I'm starting on the Kubernetes migration ticket. Wish me luck.
Good luck. I'll have the test environment ready for you by noon.
I'm going to finalize the notification center designs. Quick question — do we want to support inline images in notifications?
Let's keep v1 simple. Text only with a link to the source.
Agree. We can always add rich content later.
Makes sense. Simpler to test too.
Quick update: SSL cert renewed. Also noticed our Docker images are getting big. 1.2GB for the backend.
Yikes. Are we using a slim base image?
We're on python:3.12 which is the full image. Should switch to python:3.12-slim.
That usually cuts it in half at least
I'll make a PR for it. Also going to add a multi-stage build.
Is it lunch time yet?
It's 11:15 Dana
So... early lunch?
Ha. Let's push to noon at least.
Speaking of food, who's handling the team lunch order for Thursday?
I can do it. Same place as last time? The taco place was great.
Yes please. I want that birria quesadilla again.
The fish tacos were incredible
I'm getting the burrito bowl. Easy choice.
Alright, I'll set up the group order and share the link.
Hey quick question — is anyone using the `/api/search` endpoint? Thinking about refactoring it.
The frontend uses it for the message search feature. Why?
The query builder is really messy. I want to switch to a proper full-text search approach.
SQLite has FTS5 built in. Would be a nice improvement.
Make sure the existing behavior doesn't break. I have a bunch of tests covering edge cases.
For sure. I'll run the full test suite before and after.
Report is sent! Got good feedback from the PM already.
Nice! What did they say?
They loved the metrics section. Want us to present at the all-hands next week.
Oh cool. Who's presenting?
I vote Dana since she wrote most of it
I can do the design and metrics parts. Can someone cover the technical bits?
I'll cover the infrastructure improvements
And I'll talk about the test coverage improvements. We went from 67% to 89%.
That's a great story to tell. Let's prep slides tomorrow.
I'll set up the slide deck and share it tonight.
Heads up everyone: I'm restarting the staging server in 5 minutes for the Docker image update.
Noted. Pausing my test run.
Thanks for the warning
Staging is back up. New image is only 480MB. Down from 1.2GB.
That's a huge improvement!
Nice work Charlie
Does that affect deploy times too?
Yep, deploys went from 4 minutes to about 90 seconds
I love when infra improvements just make everything better
Ok I'm deep in the search refactor. Going heads-down for a bit.
Same, grinding through the tablet responsive bugs.
I'm in Figma if anyone needs me. Notification designs are coming along nicely.
I'll be in Terraform land. Pray for me.
Thoughts and prayers
May your state files be uncorrupted
lol
Tablet bugs are fixed. Three PRs ready for review.
I'll review them after I push my search refactor.
K8s cluster is provisioned. Tomorrow I'll start migrating services.
Notification designs are done! 12 screens total. Sharing the Figma link now.
12 screens? That's thorough.
Covers all the states: empty, loading, unread, read, error, grouped by type...
Love the attention to detail. The empty state illustration is cute.
Thanks! I spent way too long on that little bell character.
Alright I'm wrapping up. Good productive day everyone.
Same here. See you all tomorrow.
Night team! Great day.
Goodnight everyone!
Has anyone tried that new coffee place on 5th?
Yes! The cold brew is amazing
I'm more of a tea person tbh
The real question is: tabs or spaces?
oh no, not this again...
Spaces. Obviously. Fight me.
I use tabs and I'm not ashamed
I just let the formatter handle it honestly
That's the only correct answer Dana
Ok but what about semicolons in JS?
Now THAT's a real debate
No semicolons. Prettier handles it.
I add them because it feels wrong not to
Psychopath behavior
Excuse me??
Kidding! Mostly.
Anyway, what's everyone doing this weekend?
Hiking if the weather holds up
Farmers market in the morning, then probably painting
I'm going to try to beat my speedrun time on Celeste
Nice, what's your PB?
42 minutes. Trying to get under 40.
Respect. I could never.
Has anyone watched that new series on Netflix? The one about the space station?
Orbital? Yeah it's pretty good
I binged the whole thing last weekend. The ending is wild.
NO SPOILERS
I wasn't going to!
I'm on episode 3. So far so good.
It gets way better around ep 5
Ok adding it to my list
Random thought: why do we park in driveways and drive on parkways?
Please go home Bob
lol
He's got a point though
Thank you Alice. A true ally.
Speaking of random, I found the best meme about deployment yesterday
Share it!
It's a picture of a dog sitting in a burning room saying 'this is fine' with a caption 'deploying on Friday'
Accurate
Too real
We literally deployed on a Friday last week
And nothing broke! We're getting better.
Let's not jinx it
Ok lunch break. Anyone want anything from that Thai place?
Pad Thai please!
Green curry for me
I'm good, brought my lunch today
Look at Mr. Responsible over here
I'm trying to save money ok
Alright, orders noted. Back in 20.
Food is here!
You're a hero Dana
This green curry is perfect. Thank you.
I'm regretting my sad desk sandwich right now
You brought that on yourself Charlie
There's extra spring rolls if you want some
Ok twist my arm
Speaking of food takes — pineapple on pizza?
Absolutely. Hawaiian pizza is elite.
You're dead to me Bob
I'm team pineapple honestly
Same. The sweet and salty combo works.
I can't believe I work with these people
What's YOUR controversial food take Charlie?
Ketchup on eggs is perfectly fine
...that IS controversial
I mean it's not WRONG
It's a little wrong
You put pineapple on pizza, you don't get to judge me
Fair point lol
What does everyone listen to while coding? I need new music.
Lo-fi hip hop beats to study/relax to. Obviously.
I'm a movie soundtracks person. Hans Zimmer all day.
Death metal
...really?
No. Jazz mostly. Sometimes ambient electronic.
I knew the death metal was a bit
You don't know my life Bob
I went through a phase of listening to video game OSTs. The Celeste soundtrack is incredible.
Oh I love that! Also the Stardew Valley soundtrack is so cozy.
The Hades soundtrack goes hard too
Ok that one I agree with
If you want something chill, try Tycho. Great for focus mode.
Adding all of these to a playlist. Thanks everyone!
We should make a shared team playlist
Collaborative Spotify playlist? I'm in.
I'll create it. Team Vibes or something?
Call it 'Merge Conflict'
That's perfect actually
Seconded. Merge Conflict it is.
Done. Link in the team drive. Add your favorites.
Completely unrelated but my cat just knocked my coffee off the desk
Oh no! Is the laptop ok?
Laptop is fine. My dignity is not.
What's the cat's name?
Pixel. She's a menace.
Pixel is a great name for a tech person's cat
I have a corgi named Biscuit. He sits under my desk all day.
I need a photo of Biscuit immediately
Seconded
Ask and you shall receive. Check the pet channel.
WE HAVE A PET CHANNEL?
We do now. I just made one.
Best channel in this whole app
I don't have pets but I'm absolutely here for the content
Pixel photo incoming
I have two cockatiels named Git and Hub
You did NOT name your birds Git and Hub
I absolutely did
That is the most DevOps thing I've ever heard
I love it. Do they sing?
Hub knows the Mario theme. Git just screams.
Git just screams. Sounds about right.
lmaooo
Ok serious question: what's the best text editor?
VS Code. Next question.
Vim. And I will die on this hill.
How do you exit vim though?
I've been stuck in vim since 2014 and this is a cry for help
hahahaha
I use Figma for everything including writing code
Please tell me that's a joke
It is. I use VS Code like a normal person.
Normal is relative in this field
Anyone tried Zed? The new editor? It's insanely fast.
I tried it for a week. It's nice but I miss my VS Code extensions.
Extensions are golden handcuffs
What's everyone's must-have extension?
GitLens. Can't live without it.
Error Lens. Shows errors inline right in the editor.
Remote SSH. I do all my editing on remote servers.
Peacock. I color-code my editor windows by project.
That's actually genius Dana
I'm stealing that idea
Ok I'm going to force myself to do actual work now. This channel is a trap.
See you in 10 minutes when you come back
...probably
This channel is self-care Charlie
She's right. Breaks are important for productivity.
That sounds like something you'd read on a motivational poster in a WeWork
Because it was. There's one right outside the bathroom.
I'm framing that quote
Ok for real this time. Back to work. BYE.
Bye Charlie. Enjoy vim.
:wq
I hate this channel
No you don't
No I don't
Wholesome ending to a random thread. Screenshot saved.
This is going in the all-hands presentation right?
I'm working on the new auth flow. Should be done by EOD.
Can you add some integration tests for that?
Already on it. Using the new test fixtures.
Reminder: we need to update the CI pipeline for the new deps
The new login page design is ready for implementation
Thanks Dana! I'll reference those when building the UI
I found a flaky test in the message search module. Looking into it.
Was it the one that depends on timestamp ordering?
Yep, exactly. Race condition in the async handler.
I saw that one too. The fix is to use an atomic counter instead of timestamps.
That's what I was thinking. PR incoming.
Make sure to add a regression test for it
Way ahead of you
Question: should the error states use red or our warning orange?
Red for errors, orange for warnings. Let's keep them distinct.
Makes sense. I'll update the component library.
The new monitoring dashboard is up btw. Check grafana.internal/dashboards
Ooh nice. I can see the request latency graphs.
p99 is at 120ms. Not bad but we should aim for under 100.
Most of the latency is in the DB queries. We need to add some indexes.
I can profile the slow queries this afternoon
That would be great. Start with the message search endpoint — that one's the worst.
Also the room list query does a full table scan when you have 50+ rooms
Yikes. Ok I'll look at both.
While we're on performance — the frontend bundle is 2.3MB. Can we tree-shake some of that?
Yeah, I noticed we're importing all of lodash when we only use like 3 functions.
Classic
Just import what you need: import debounce from 'lodash/debounce'
I'll do a pass on the imports this sprint
That should help. Also the SVG icons are huge — we should switch to an icon font or sprite sheet.
Good idea. Let's add that to the sprint backlog.
PR #247 is ready for review. It's the WebSocket reconnection logic.
I'll take a look
Me too. How did you handle the backoff?
Exponential backoff with jitter. Starts at 1s, maxes at 30s.
That's the right approach. Does it preserve the subscription state?
Yep, it replays room.join for all previously joined rooms on reconnect.
Nice. What about messages that arrived while disconnected?
It uses the ?since= parameter to fetch anything missed.
LGTM. Approving.
Same, looks solid. One minor nit on the variable naming but not blocking.
I'll fix that before merging. Thanks for the quick review!
Hey, the A/B test results for the new onboarding are in.
And?
Variant B (the simplified form) wins by a huge margin. 40% better completion rate.
Wow that's massive
Ship it.
Agreed. Let's make variant B the default.
Already updated the feature flag. Rolling out to 100% now.
I'll remove the old variant code in a cleanup PR
Don't forget to remove the feature flag config too
Yep, I'll clean up the whole thing
One more thing — we should update the API docs. The new endpoints aren't documented yet.
I can do that. Which endpoints are missing?
The room folder endpoints and the new plugin API.
On it. Should have the docs updated by tomorrow.
I'll add example requests/responses to the test suite too. Those double as docs.
The swagger UI already auto-generates a lot of it. Just needs descriptions.
True. I'll focus on the descriptions and examples then.
Great. I think that covers everything for today's standup.
Shortest standup ever. Love it.
Efficient team is efficient
Back to coding then. Talk later!
One sec — anyone want to pair on the caching layer this afternoon?
I'm in. 2pm work?
Perfect. I'll set up the branch.
Can I sit in? Want to understand the caching strategy for the test suite.
Of course. The more eyes the better.
I'll skip the pairing but let me know if you need any UI for cache invalidation controls.
Will do. We might need a 'clear cache' button in the admin panel.
Easy. I'll have a mockup ready by tomorrow.
Alright, see everyone at 2. Going to grab lunch.
Ok the pairing session went great. We've got a two-layer cache: in-memory LRU + Redis.
The LRU handles hot data, Redis handles the warm tier. Invalidation is event-driven.
I learned a ton watching you two work through that. The cache stampede protection is clever.
Yeah the lock-and-recompute pattern is key. Prevents thundering herd on cache misses.
Did you end up needing that admin UI for cache controls?
Definitely. We want a button to flush specific cache namespaces.
I'll prioritize the mockup. Should have it by EOD.
I'm writing the cache integration tests now. How should I handle cache warmup in the test fixtures?
Use a separate Redis DB for tests. I'll add the config. Just use REDIS_DB=1 for tests.
Also make sure to flush between test runs so there's no bleed.
Good point. I'll add that to the conftest.
Found something weird. When a user leaves a room and rejoins, their unread count is wrong.
Wrong how? Too high or too low?
Too high. It's counting messages from when they weren't a member.
That's probably the membership timestamp not being updated on rejoin.
Let me check... yeah, the rejoin path just sets status='active' but doesn't update joined_at.
So the unread query uses joined_at to filter, but it's the original join date, not the rejoin date.
Exactly. Easy fix. We need to update joined_at on rejoin. One line change.
Should we also store the leave timestamp? Might be useful for audit trails.
That's a good idea but let's scope this fix small. Just the joined_at update.
Agreed. I'll file a separate ticket for the leave audit trail.
PR is up. #252. It's literally a one-line diff.
Reviewing... LGTM. Clean fix.
Approved. Merge it.
Merged. Bob can you verify the fix?
Testing now... unread count is correct after rejoin. Ship it.
Heads up: I ran a dependency audit this morning. We have 3 medium vulnerabilities.
In what packages?
Two in transitive deps of the markdown parser, one in the old version of pyjwt.
pyjwt is easy. Just bump the version.
Already did that one. The markdown parser ones are trickier. Upstream hasn't patched yet.
What kind of vulns? XSS?
One is a ReDoS in the regex parser. The other is an HTML injection in the sanitizer.
We should switch to markdown-it. It's been more actively maintained.
That's a bigger change though. Want to timebox it?
Fair. Let's give it half a day. If it's not clean by then, we pin and revisit next sprint.
I'll handle the migration. The API is similar so it shouldn't be too bad.
Will the rendering change at all? I don't want the message formatting to look different.
Shouldn't. I'll do a visual comparison before and after.
Thanks. Let me know if you need me to check anything.
Profile results are in for the slow queries. Message search is doing a sequential scan on 500k rows.
Oof. We definitely need that FTS5 index.
How big is the messages table right now?
About 500k rows, 200MB on disk. Not huge but the queries are still slow without indexes.
FTS5 virtual table should handle this nicely. I'll set it up with triggers to keep it in sync.
Make sure to use the unicode61 tokenizer so non-ASCII search works.
Good call. I almost forgot about that.
The room list query was also bad. Added an index on room_members(username, room_id) and it went from 800ms to 2ms.
That's a 400x improvement. Wow.
Indexes are magic. Until you have too many of them.
PR #253 for the room list index. Should I include the FTS migration too?
No, keep them separate. FTS is a bigger change. I'll put it in its own PR.
Question about the notification API: should dismissed notifications disappear permanently or just be marked as read?
Marked as read. Users might want to go back and find them.
Agree. Permanent deletion makes me nervous from a UX perspective.
From a data perspective, soft delete is better too. We can always purge old ones in a background job.
Makes sense. I'll add a 'show dismissed' toggle to the UI.
Nice. Let's also add a 'mark all as read' button. That's always useful.
And a 'dismiss all' for the bold ones among us
Inbox zero energy
Love it. Updated the mockups.
I'm looking at the notification data model now. We'll need: id, user_id, type, title, body, link, read_at, dismissed_at, created_at
Add a source_id and source_type too. So we can link back to the message or event that triggered it.
Good thinking. Polymorphic source reference. I'll add that.
Don't forget the delivery preferences. Users might want to disable certain notification types.
That's a separate table. notification_preferences with user_id, type, enabled, created_at.
Should I design a notification preferences page too?
Yes please. Put it in Settings > Notifications.
On it.
Markdown parser migration is done. PR #254. Rendering looks identical.
Reviewing now. The diff is surprisingly clean.
Tests all pass. Nice work Charlie.
Thanks. The new parser is also 3x faster. Unexpected bonus.
Approved. Let's merge and deploy tomorrow morning after a soak test overnight on staging.
Smart. I'll deploy to staging now and we can check it first thing tomorrow.
I set up a load test to run against staging overnight. 10 req/s for 8 hours.
That's thorough. Should catch any memory leaks.
Notification preferences mockup is done. Six screens. Sharing now.
That was fast!
I had a head start from the settings page patterns we already established.
These look great Dana. The toggle grouping by category is really intuitive.
Can we get a 'quiet hours' feature in there too? I don't want pings at 2am.
Adding it. Good idea.
If Charlie's getting paged at 2am we have bigger problems
You'd be surprised
Alright, wrapping up. Pushed the FTS5 PR. It can wait for review tomorrow.
I'll review first thing. My overnight load test is running so I'm heading out too.
Same. Staging deploy is done. Fingers crossed for a clean overnight.
Night everyone! Don't forget we have the all-hands prep tomorrow at 11.
Night! Good reminder, I'll prep my slides tonight.
Later all!
See you tomorrow. Don't let the bugs bite.
